description: List the events with the largest share of attendance records down to the 10th place, including every event tied with the 10th.

c.request: What are the top 10 events by share of total attendance? For each one, give the event id, its number of attendance records, and its share of all attendance records (its count divided by the total, unrounded), from the largest share down, and return nothing if there's no total to divide by. List the events with the largest share of attendance records down to the 10th place, including every event tied with the 10th.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM attendance), ranked AS (SELECT c.event_id, c.attendance_count, CAST(c.attendance_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CAST(c.attendance_count AS REAL) / t.total_count DESC) AS rnk FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_count > 0) SELECT event_id, attendance_count, share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC;

b.request: List the top 10 events by attendance-record share (count of attendance rows per event_id divided by total attendance rows, unrounded, descending), including all events tied with the 10th-place share, and return no rows if the total attendance count is zero
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cnt FROM attendance), shares AS (SELECT c.event_id, CAST(c.cnt AS REAL) / t.total_cnt AS share FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_cnt > 0), ranked AS (SELECT event_id, share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM shares) SELECT event_id, share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC;

a.request: For each event in the attendance records (`attendance.link_to_event`), how many attendance records does it have, and what share of all attendance records is that (its count divided by the total of all per-event counts, unrounded; nothing is returned if that total is missing)? Return the event id, its count and its share, sorted by share from highest to lowest with missing values last. Keep the first 10 rows plus any further events whose share ties with the 10th one.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM attendance WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event), shares AS (SELECT event_id, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM counts), ranked AS (SELECT event_id, cnt, share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM shares) SELECT event_id, cnt, share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY (share IS NULL), share DESC;

d.request: Which events have the largest share of attendance records, listed from largest share downward through 10th place, including every event tied with the 10th-place share? For each event, give the event id, its number of attendance records, and its share of all attendance records (its count divided by the total, unrounded). Return nothing if there is no total to divide by.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM attendance), ranked AS (SELECT c.event_id, c.attendance_count, CAST(c.attendance_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY c.attendance_count DESC) AS rnk FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE t.total_count > 0) SELECT event_id, attendance_count, share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY attendance_count DESC, event_id;
